title: Best BI tools for combining data from multiple sources (2026): 9 tools compared on blending, joins, and connectors
summary: Power BI, Qlik, Domo, and Zoho join sources in their own engines, Data Studio blends up to five, and Metabase needs one database. 9 multi-source tools compared.
body_markdown:
The BI tools that combine data from multiple sources most directly in November 2026 are Power BI, Qlik Cloud Analytics, Domo, and Zoho Analytics, because each one imports data from many connectors into its own engine and lets you join it there. Tableau and Data Studio can also join or blend across sources, with documented limits, and Databox merges synced datasets for KPI dashboards. Basedash joins live query results from several databases in one chart (in beta) or syncs SaaS data into a managed warehouse, while Metabase and Sigma only join within one database, so they work best once your data sits in a single warehouse.


## How we evaluated multi-source BI tools


We read each vendor’s official documentation and pricing pages on November 25, 2026, and compared nine tools on five criteria taken from the questions buyers ask about combining data:


1. **How the tool combines sources:** imported into its own engine, joined at query time, blended at the chart level, or only after you centralize data in a warehouse.
2. **Documented limits:** how many sources a blend can hold, which join types work, which connectors are excluded, and row caps.
3. **Connectors and freshness:** published connector counts and how often imported data refreshes on each plan.
4. **Who can build the combined view:** whether non-technical users can combine sources without SQL, and whether AI can do it for them.
5. **Security and price:** row-level security, SAML SSO, and SCIM, plus the starting price.


We didn’t run hands-on tests. Every limit below is the vendor’s own published number. For background on the three underlying approaches (centralizing in a warehouse, query federation, and blending), see our explainer on[how BI tools combine data from multiple sources](https://www.basedash.com/blog/how-bi-tools-combine-data-from-multiple-sources-federation-blending-and-warehouses) .

## Power BI: best for Microsoft shops that model data from many systems


**Best for:** teams on Microsoft 365 and Azure with an analyst who can build a semantic model in Power Query. **Not ideal for:** business users who want to combine sources without learning modeling, or companies outside Microsoft identity.


- **Pricing:** Pro is $14 and Premium Per User is $24 per user per month, paid yearly ([Power BI pricing](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi/pricing) ). A free account can build reports but not share them; a 30-day Pro trial covers up to 25 licenses. Verified November 2026.
- **How it combines sources:** Power Query[merges](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/merge-queries-overview) tables from any connected source with left outer, right outer, full outer, inner, and anti joins, plus fuzzy matching on text columns.[Composite models](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-composite-models) mix Import, DirectQuery, and Direct Lake tables, but relationships across DirectQuery source groups “are always limited relationships,” which restricts some calculations.
- **Refresh:** imported models refresh up to 8 times a day on shared capacity and 48 times on PPU or Fabric capacity ([refresh docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/refresh-data) ).
- **Security:**[row-level security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/enterprise/service-admin-rls) applies only to users with Viewer permissions, not workspace Admins, Members, or Contributors. Sign-in runs through Microsoft Entra ID.
- **AI:** Copilot needs F2 or higher Fabric capacity or P1 or higher Premium; a Pro or PPU license alone isn’t enough ([Copilot requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/copilot-introduction) ). The report agent pane is generally available, and Q&A goes away in February 2027.
- **Embedding:** “Embed for your customers” requires a capacity in production ([embedded analytics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/developer/embedded/embedded-analytics-power-bi) ).
- **Tradeoff:** Power BI is flexible, but combining sources is modeling work. Without someone who owns the model, merges multiply across reports.


## Tableau: best for analysts who mix relationships, joins, and blends


**Best for:** analyst teams that combine a warehouse with spreadsheets or a second database and want visual control over how. **Not ideal for:** combining extract-only marketing sources with each other, or small teams on a tight budget.


- **Pricing:** Standard starts at $15 and Enterprise at $35 per user per month, billed annually, and “every deployment requires at least one Creator license” ([Tableau pricing](https://www.tableau.com/pricing) ). Tableau Desktop Free Edition can’t publish. Verified November 2026.
- **How it combines sources:**[relationships](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/joining_tables.htm) are the default and keep each table’s level of detail. Cross-database joins support inner, left, right, and full outer joins but exclude cube data, “most extract-only data (e.g., Google Analytics and OData),” and published data sources.[Data blending](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/multiple_connections.htm) queries each source separately and works like a left join, but “data from secondary data sources must always be aggregated” and a blend can’t be published as a unit.
- **Connectors and refresh:** Tableau lists “60+ native database and data application connectors” ([Tableau data](https://www.tableau.com/enterprise-it/data) ). Tableau Cloud gives each site up to 8 backgrounder hours per Creator license per day for extract refreshes ([site capacity](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/to_site_capacity.htm) ).
- **Security:**[row-level security](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/rls_options_overview.htm) through user filters or data policies (the latter need Data Management). SAML and SCIM are documented for Tableau Cloud.
- **AI:** Tableau Agent in web authoring requires Tableau+ or Tableau Cloud+ ([Tableau Agent FAQ](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/web_author_einstein_faq.htm) ).
- **Embedding:**[Embedding API v3](https://help.tableau.com/current/api/embedding_api/en-us/index.html) .
- **Tradeoff:** three mechanisms with different rules means analysts need to know which one a workbook uses. Tableau Prep is the cleaner path for recurring cross-source logic.


## Qlik Cloud Analytics: best for associative models across many sources


**Best for:** teams that want every source loaded into one model where selections filter across all of it. **Not ideal for:** teams that need live queries across several databases at once.


- **Pricing:** Starter is $300 per month for 10 users; Standard is $825 per month for 25 GB of data with unlimited users; Premium is $2,750 per month for 50 GB; Enterprise is quote only. All billed annually ([Qlik pricing](https://www.qlik.com/us/pricing) ). 30-day trial, no card. Verified November 2026.
- **How it combines sources:** the load script, written in the Data load editor or generated by Data manager, “defines what data to load and how to link the different loaded tables” ([Qlik help](https://help.qlik.com/en-US/cloud-services/Subsystems/Hub/Content/Sense_Hub/Scripting/synthetic-keys.htm) ). In scripts, fields with the same name in different tables associate automatically.[Direct Query](https://help.qlik.com/en-US/cloud-services/Subsystems/Hub/Content/Sense_Hub/DirectQuery/limitations-direct-query.htm) apps “can only use a single database” and return at most 1 million rows per query.
- **Limits:** in-memory app size is 5 GB on Starter and Standard, 10 GB on Premium, and 15 GB on Enterprise, with a 3-hour reload limit ([capacity specs](https://help.qlik.com/en-US/cloud-services/Subsystems/Hub/Content/Sense_Hub/Introduction/qcs-specs-capacity.htm) ).
- **Security:**[section access](https://help.qlik.com/en-US/cloud-services/Subsystems/Hub/Content/Sense_Hub/Scripting/Security/manage-security-with-section-access.htm) restricts rows, columns, or both. SAML or OIDC sign-in; SCIM is documented for Microsoft Entra ID.
- **AI:** Qlik Answers replaces Insight Advisor, and every plan includes a monthly Qlik Answers question allowance and the MCP server ([Qlik pricing](https://www.qlik.com/us/pricing) ).
- **Embedding:**[qlik-embed](https://qlik.dev/embed/qlik-embed/) web components for Qlik Cloud and client-managed Qlik Sense.
- **Tradeoff:** load scripts are a Qlik-specific skill, and the data is a copy refreshed on reload, not live.


## Domo: best for connector-heavy teams that want ETL and dashboards in one product


**Best for:** companies pulling dozens of SaaS tools into one place without a separate ETL vendor. **Not ideal for:** teams that need a published price before talking to sales.


- **Pricing:** credit-based with “no per-user charges” and custom pricing; 30-day trial with no credit card ([Domo pricing](https://www.domo.com/pricing) ). Verified November 2026.
- **How it combines sources:** Domo lists “1K+ pre-built connectors” ([connectors](https://www.domo.com/data-integration/connectors) ). The Magic ETL Join Data tile combines two DataSets on common values ([Magic ETL docs](https://www.domo.com/docs/s/article/360044876194) ); DataFusion “has been deprecated” in favor of Magic ETL. Cloud Integrations (Cloud Amplifier on the pricing page) read, write back, and push queries down to Snowflake, with pushdown in beta for BigQuery and Databricks, but views that join a Cloud Integrations DataSet with a Domo DataSet aren’t supported ([Cloud Integrations](https://www.domo.com/docs/s/article/4412849158167) ).
- **Security:**[row policies and column masking](https://www.domo.com/docs/s/article/360042934614) , SAML and OIDC, and SCIM ([SSO docs](https://www.domo.com/docs/s/article/000005827) ).
- **AI:** from November 1, 2026, AI chat consumes credits as part of Domo AI Pro at 0.01 credits per operation ([consumption terms](https://www.domo.com/consumption-terms) ).
- **Embedding:**[Domo Embed](https://www.domo.com/embedded-analytics) , with user-based, server-based, and platform-based private embedding.
- **Tradeoff:** credits cover data, ETL, and AI together, so forecasting cost depends on how much you sync and transform.


## Zoho Analytics: best low-cost option for blending SaaS apps


**Best for:** small and mid-size companies combining Zoho apps, Shopify, and ad platforms on a budget. **Not ideal for:** live querying across several warehouses or SCIM-based provisioning.


- **Pricing:** Basic $24 (2 users), Standard $48 (5 users), Premium $115 (15 users), and Enterprise $455 (50 users) per month billed annually; free plan with 2 users and 10,000 rows; 15-day trial ([Zoho Analytics pricing](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/pricing.html) ). Verified November 2026.
- **How it combines sources:** Zoho lists “500+ connectors” ([Zoho Analytics](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/) ).[Data blending](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/help/datablending.html) uses lookup columns across sources in the same workspace, and[auto-join](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/help/table/joining-tables.html) joins tables linked by lookups when you build a report.[Query Tables](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/help/query-tables.html) support left, right, and inner joins in SQL.
- **Refresh:** imported data refreshes once a day on Basic, 8 times on Standard and Premium, and 24 times on Enterprise.[Live Connect](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/help/datasources/live-connect.html) is Premium and Enterprise only, and live sources can’t use lookups to other sources.
- **Security:** row filters when sharing views ([sharing docs](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/help/sharing/sharing-to-a-user.html) ) and SAML 2.0 through[Zoho Directory](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/help/zoho-directory.html) . SCIM isn’t documented.
- **AI:** Ask Zia’s Analysis, SQL, Formula, and Visualization agents are available on every plan including Free ([AI settings](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/help/account-setup/ai-settings.html) ).
- **Embedding:** embed snippets, an embed API, a JavaScript SDK, and a white-label portal ([embedded analytics](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/embedded/ai-powered-embedded-analytics.html) ).
- **Tradeoff:** the cheaper plans refresh imported data only once or eight times a day.


## Data Studio: best free option for blending Google marketing data


**Best for:** marketing teams combining Google Ads, GA4, Sheets, and BigQuery in shareable reports. **Not ideal for:** joins across more than five sources, or anything needing SAML.


- **Pricing:** free for creators and viewers; Data Studio Pro is $9 per user per project per month ([Data Studio](https://cloud.google.com/looker-studio) ), with a 30-day Pro trial. Verified November 2026.
- **How it combines sources:** “you can blend up to five distinct data sources” with inner, left outer, right outer, full outer, and cross joins, plus union. Joins only support equality conditions, blends live inside the report that created them, and metrics become unaggregated dimensions in the blend ([blending docs](https://support.google.com/looker-studio/answer/9061420) ). Google says Data Studio connects to “more than 1,400 data sources.”
- **Freshness:** Google marketing products refresh every 12 hours; BigQuery defaults to 12 hours and can go down to 1 minute; a blend uses the slowest refresh of its sources ([data freshness](https://support.google.com/looker-studio/answer/7020039) ).
- **Security:**[filter by email](https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-studio/filter-by-email-address) works on any data source. SAML and SCIM aren’t documented.
- **AI:** Conversational Analytics became generally available on July 30, 2026, and runs on data agents created in BigQuery ([release notes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-studio/release-notes) ).
- **Embedding:** iframe embeds always show the Data Studio watermark ([embed docs](https://support.google.com/looker-studio/answer/7450249) ).
- **Tradeoff:** every blend is rebuilt per report, so shared definitions drift across reports.


## Databox: best for KPI dashboards across many SaaS tools


**Best for:** teams and agencies tracking KPIs from marketing, sales, and finance tools on one screen. **Not ideal for:** row-level analysis or joining raw tables from a production database.


- **Pricing:** Business is $399 per month billed annually or $499 monthly, for up to 10 users and 30 data sources; Custom starts at $15,000. No free plan; 14-day trial with no card ([Databox pricing](https://databox.com/pricing) ). Verified November 2026.
- **How it combines sources:** Databox connects to “130+ tools, plus your databases, spreadsheets, and APIs” ([integrations](https://databox.com/integrations) ).[Merged datasets](https://help.databox.com/merge-datasets) combine up to 20 datasets with left outer, inner, right outer, or full outer joins, up to 150 columns.
- **Refresh:** Databox stores synced metric data, and the plan sets the maximum refresh rate ([data sync](https://help.databox.com/data-sync-storage-security-in-databox) ); a 15-minute sync add-on is available.
- **Security:** SAML 2.0 SSO comes with the $40 per month Advanced security add-on. Row-level security and SCIM aren’t documented.
- **AI:** Genie, AI Analyst, and an MCP server run on monthly AI credits (1,500 on Business).
- **Embedding:** dashboards embed on websites and client portals ([sharing docs](https://help.databox.com/share-a-dashboard) ); white-labeling is an $80 per month add-on.
- **Tradeoff:** Databox is metric-first. It is fast for KPIs but not built for ad hoc questions across raw tables.


## Basedash: best for small teams joining a production database with SaaS data, with AI writing the SQL


**Best for:** startups and mid-size companies that want plain-English questions across a live Postgres or Snowflake database and synced Stripe, HubSpot, or Shopify data. **Not ideal for:** heavy row-level security across every source, teams that want a free plan, or visual join builders without SQL underneath.


- **Pricing:** Startup is $1,000 per month plus AI usage for up to 25 users, with $1,000 per month in AI credits; Enterprise is custom ([Basedash pricing](https://www.basedash.com/pricing) ). 14-day free trial, no card. Verified November 2026.
- **How it combines sources:**[multi-source charts](https://www.basedash.com/docs/features/multi-source-charts) run one query per data source and join the results in DuckDB. They’re in beta and enabled on request, with up to 8 source queries per chart, 50,000 rows and 25 MB per source, and no drilldowns or export. For recurring work,[Basedash Warehouse](https://www.basedash.com/features/warehouse) syncs[750+ SaaS sources](https://www.basedash.com/features/data-ingestion) through Fivetran every 15 minutes to 24 hours, where they can be joined in one SQL query.
- **Query model:** connected[databases and warehouses](https://www.basedash.com/docs/data-sources/introduction) (including Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake, BigQuery, ClickHouse, and Databricks) are queried live.
- **Security:** each source query keeps its data source access rules and RLS.[Row-level security](https://www.basedash.com/docs/administration/row-level-security) is Postgres and Supabase only, and DuckDB-based Basedash Warehouses don’t support it. SSO (SAML or OIDC) and SCIM are Enterprise features.
- **AI:** the[AI data analyst](https://www.basedash.com/features/ai-data-analyst) writes the source queries and the join query when multi-source charts are enabled, and shows the SQL it ran.
- **Embedding:** Enterprise only ([embedding docs](https://www.basedash.com/docs/developers/embedding) ).
- **Tradeoff:** cross-source joins are SQL-based and capped by row limits, so aggregate in each source first. Domo and Zoho offer drag-and-drop ETL instead.


## Metabase: best once your data already sits in one warehouse


**Best for:** teams with a single warehouse or database that want open-source, self-hosted BI. **Not ideal for:** joining two production databases or SaaS APIs directly.


- **Pricing:** open source is free; Starter is $100 per month with 5 users (plus $6 per user), Pro is $575 per month with 10 users (plus $12 per user), and Enterprise starts at $20,000 per year ([Metabase pricing](https://www.metabase.com/pricing/) ). 14-day Cloud trial. Verified November 2026.
- **How it combines sources:** in the query builder “you can only pick tables and saved questions that are from the same database as your starting data” ([joins docs](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/questions/query-builder/join) ), and[transforms](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/data-studio/transforms/transforms-overview) can’t write from one database to another. Metabase Cloud can store CSV uploads and Google Sheets, with the first million rows free.
- **Security:** row and column security, SAML, and SCIM are Pro and Enterprise only.
- **AI:**[Metabot](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/ai/metabot) is available on every plan, including open source with your own API key.
- **Embedding:** guest embeds on every plan; the modular embedding SDK for React on Pro and Enterprise.
- **Tradeoff:** you need an ETL tool and a warehouse first. Sigma has the same rule (“you cannot join tables across connections”) per its[join docs](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/join-types) . Our[data integration tools comparison](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-data-integration-tools-compared-2026) covers the pipeline side.


## Which multi-source BI tool should you choose?


**Your ecommerce team needs Shopify, Google Ads, and a warehouse in one place, built by non-technical merchandisers.** Zoho Analytics has[Shopify](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/shopify-analytics.html) and[Google Ads](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/help/connectors/google-ads.html) connectors and lets business users join through lookups. Databox suits KPI tracking from the same sources. Basedash syncs[Shopify](https://www.basedash.com/data-sources/shopify) and[Google Ads](https://www.basedash.com/data-sources/google-ads) into its warehouse and answers questions in plain English. Our[ecommerce analytics comparison](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-ecommerce-analytics-tools-compared-2026) goes deeper.


**You’re a startup that needs multiple sources, row-level security, and no SQL.** Zoho Analytics is the cheapest place to start. Metabase Pro and Basedash both cover RLS, with Basedash limited to Postgres and Supabase. See our[row-level security comparison](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-bi-tools-for-row-level-security-compared-2026) .


**You need a customer 360 dashboard across different database systems.** Tableau cross-database joins, Power BI composite models, and Basedash multi-source charts can join live databases without a pipeline. Past a few tables, centralize in a warehouse; our guide to a[customer 360 view without a CDP](https://www.basedash.com/blog/how-to-build-a-customer-360-view-without-a-cdp) walks through it.


**You don’t have a warehouse and don’t want one yet.** Domo, Qlik, and Zoho act as the storage layer. Basedash Warehouse is a managed option inside the BI tool; our[Basedash vs Domo comparison](https://www.basedash.com/vs/basedash-vs-domo) puts the two side by side.


**You already have Snowflake or BigQuery.** Load every source there and use Metabase, Sigma, or Basedash on top, so joins run in one place and definitions don’t split across reports.


## Frequently asked questions


### Which BI tools can combine data from multiple sources without a data warehouse?


Domo, Qlik Cloud Analytics, and Zoho Analytics store imported data themselves, so they combine sources without a separate warehouse. Domo joins DataSets in Magic ETL, Qlik links tables in its load script, and Zoho uses lookup columns and SQL Query Tables. Tableau and Power BI can also join across sources in an extract or an imported model. Data Studio blends up to five sources per chart with no storage of its own. Basedash includes a managed warehouse that syncs 750+ SaaS sources, so you don’t have to run one.


### Which analytics platforms handle multi-source blending for Shopify, Google Ads, and a data warehouse?


Zoho Analytics, Databox, and Basedash all document Shopify and Google Ads connectors and can combine them with warehouse data. Zoho imports everything and lets business users join it through lookup columns, with no SQL. Databox merges up to 20 synced datasets for KPI dashboards. Basedash syncs Shopify and Google Ads into Basedash Warehouse and lets merchandisers ask questions in plain English. Domo’s 1,000+ connectors and Magic ETL suit larger teams, and Data Studio blends Google Ads with BigQuery for free, up to five sources per blend.


### What BI platforms connect to multiple data sources, have row-level security, and don’t require SQL?


Zoho Analytics, Domo, Qlik Cloud Analytics, and Power BI all pair many connectors with row-level security and visual builders. Zoho is the least expensive, with paid plans from $24 per month and row filters applied when you share a view. Metabase offers row and column security on Pro and Enterprise, but can’t join across databases. Basedash covers no-SQL users through its AI data analyst, but its row-level security works only on Postgres and Supabase, and SSO and SCIM need the Enterprise plan.


### Can AI build reports from multiple data sources?


Some tools can. Basedash’s chat writes one query per source plus the join query when multi-source charts are enabled. Databox’s Genie works across all data in a Databox account. Zoho’s Ask Zia agents answer questions on data already combined in a workspace. Most AI assistants, including Power BI Copilot and Qlik Answers, work on a model that someone has already combined, so the joining still happens in the data model first.


### How many data sources can you blend in Data Studio (Looker Studio)?


Google’s documentation says you can blend up to five distinct data sources in one blend. Blends support inner, left outer, right outer, full outer, and cross joins, plus union, and join conditions must use equality. Each blend lives inside the report where you built it, so other reports can’t reuse it. Data freshness for a blend follows the slowest refresh among its sources, and Google marketing sources refresh every 12 hours. For more than five sources, load them into BigQuery and connect Data Studio to that.


### Can Metabase join data from two different databases?


No. Metabase’s query builder only lets you join tables and saved questions from the same database as your starting data, and Metabase transforms can’t write from one database to another. Teams that need cross-database joins either replicate both databases into one warehouse with an ETL tool and point Metabase at it, or upload smaller datasets as CSVs or Google Sheets into Metabase Cloud’s built-in storage. Sigma has the same rule: it can’t join tables across connections.
